description: Canonical AI-tell rule table for prose-audit. Loaded by science-agent/prose-audit.js. Engine-specific rules (custom traversal) are declared here for discoverability; their detectors live in code.
notes: v6 (2026-08-22): added 5 rules restoring coverage removed by the v2/v3 licence purges, re-derived from MIT-licensed sources — copula-avoidance, significance-inflation, participial-significance-tail, actorless-evidence (actorless/anthropomorphic claims) and weasel-attribution (uncited authority claims, citation-aware). v5 (2026-05-19): added 3 fragment-detection rules (fragment-discourse-marker, fragment-participial, fragment-relative-clause) addressing non-sentence-sentence patterns identified during AllSERP paper cleanup. v4 added 4 proselint-derived BSD-3-Clause rules. v3 removed CC-BY-SA-4.0; v2 removed CC BY-NC 4.0.

rules.message_template: Em-dash #{n} of {total}. Limit is ≤{limit} per paper. Replace with commas, parentheses, or separate sentences.
rules.source: first-party observation (allserp-paper/paper.tex draft had 13 em-dashes; cleanup target = ≤3)

rules.message_template: Semicolon #{n} of {total} ({rate}/1000 words; limit {limit}/1000). Use a period or restructure into parallel clauses.
rules.source: first-party observation (allserp-paper/paper.tex draft had 20 semicolons; cleanup target = ≤2/1000w)

rules.description: Fires when 'Not X. Y.' / 'Not just X — Y' patterns exceed the per-paper limit. Detector implementation lives in prose-audit.js.
rules.source: first-party observation (allserp-paper/paper.tex had 'Two flavors, two stories' flagged as binary-contrast tic)

rules.message: Leaked OpenAI tool-citation token. Strip before any external pass.
Leaked LLM tool token (turn-N). Always real; strip immediately.
Leaked OpenAI sandbox path. Always real.
Live ChatGPT URL embedded in prose. Always a paste artifact.
Citation copied from ChatGPT with tracking parameter intact.
Knowledge-cutoff disclaimer is LLM throat-clearing; cut.
LLM real-time-data disclaimer; cut.
Refusal/preamble residue from an LLM session. Strip.
Folksy where the rest is technical. Replace with something specific.
Definitional cleft tic. Use 'where X happens' or just name X.
Definitional cleft tic. Most uses can become 'where X is recorded' or 'X-level'.
Performative depth. Say 'the partition is grounded in' or just state the grounding.
Anthropomorphism reviewers will quote back at you. Drop or rephrase mechanically.
Self-conscious framing. Trust the metaphor or unpack it plainly.
Title-explainer tic. Cut or rewrite as plain English.
Authorial-voice hedging that weakens the close. State what the work does.
Italicized motif. Allowed once (e.g., §5 header). Flag every additional occurrence.
Title aside is overwrought. Trust the title or unpack plainly.
'This is not just X — it's Y' escalation. Tell of LLM rhetoric. Convert to plain claim.
'Regime' carries political connotations in current usage; for technical contexts prefer 'phase', 'mode', or 'state'.
rules.notes: Suppressed in technical collocations (asymptotic / linear / scotopic / saturation regime), which are neutral vocabulary in physics, applied maths and vision science. Only the political sense is a tell. Ported from muriel.aiism RULE_SUPPRESS: without it the native engine fired on domain terms in .tex, where muriel never runs to suppress them.

rules.message: Meme phrase. Use one place where the metaphor pulls weight; replace others with 'central', 'primary', 'defended claim'.
Empty intensifier. Either give the number that justifies it or drop the adverb.
Empty intensifier. Either give the number or drop the adverb.
Empty intensifier. Either give the number or drop the adverb.
Already-Y compound used many times. Vary phrasing; 'previously', 'prior', plain past tense work too.
Doubled 'What X is Y' cleft (two within close range). Sharper tell than single use; convert at least one to plain subject-verb.

rules.description: Long-sentence detector. Sentence ≥ warn_at_words → info; ≥ error_at_words → warn. Detector requires per-line splitter; implemented in each engine.
Flags paragraphs with ≥3 bold spans. Requires markdown-aware paragraph segmentation; implemented in each engine.
Flags lines with ≥3 em/en dashes. Per-line scan; implemented in each engine.

rules.pattern: \b(?:The (?:preceding|preceeding) (?:discussion|paragraph (?:demonstrated|showed))|The rest of this article|This (?:chapter|section) (?:discusses|analyzes|examines)|The previous section analyzed)\b
rules.message: Excessive metadiscourse. Cut the meta-commentary and write the thing.

rules.pattern: \bIn recent years,?\s+an increasing number of [a-zA-Z]{3,}sts have\b
rules.message: Professional narcissism. Talk about the subject, not its study.

rules.pattern: \b(?:I would argue that|to a certain degree),?\s*
rules.message: Hedging. State the claim directly.
Excessive apologizing. State what's known and what's open instead.

Possible sentence fragment: discourse marker (Such as / Including / Importantly / etc.) followed by short clause ending in '.'. Either splice into the previous sentence, replace the period with a comma, or rewrite as a full sentence.
rules.source: first-party observation (AllSERP cleanup); fragment patterns common to AI/academic prose

rules.message: Possible sentence fragment: participial phrase (Resulting in / Following / Given / Based on / etc.) as standalone sentence. Attach to a main clause or convert to active voice with a subject.
rules.source: first-party observation (AllSERP cleanup); standard fragment pattern in academic prose

rules.message: Possible sentence fragment: relative clause (Which / That / Who / etc.) as standalone sentence. Relative clauses are dependent — splice into the previous sentence with a comma, or restart with a subject.
rules.source: first-party observation (AllSERP cleanup); standard fragment pattern

rules.message: Standalone discourse-adverb as 'sentence' (e.g. 'Importantly.' / 'Notably.'). Attach to the following sentence: 'Importantly, X is Y.'
Copula avoidance. 'is' or 'has' is usually the clearer verb. Keep only where the thing literally performs the function named (a component that serves a request).
rules.source: MIT-licensed skill corpus (stop-slop, deslop, no-ai-slop, elithrar/anti-slop — see aiism-rules.LICENSE.md)

rules.message: Significance inflation. Asserts that something matters instead of showing the consequence. State the specific result and let the reader weigh it.
rules.source: MIT-licensed skill corpus (stop-slop, deslop, no-ai-slop, elithrar/anti-slop — see aiism-rules.LICENSE.md)

rules.message: Participial tail asserting significance. The clause adds interpretation, not evidence. Cut it, or replace with the concrete consequence.
rules.notes: Deliberately excludes demonstrating / illustrating / showing / reflecting / ensuring: those carry real result content in scientific prose and firing on them costs more precision than the rule is worth.
rules.source: MIT-licensed skill corpus (stop-slop, deslop, no-ai-slop, elithrar/anti-slop — see aiism-rules.LICENSE.md)

rules.message: Actorless claim. Data does not tell and decisions do not emerge; a person read something and concluded something. Name the analysis or the author.
rules.source: MIT-licensed skill corpus (stop-slop, deslop, no-ai-slop, elithrar/anti-slop — see aiism-rules.LICENSE.md)

rules.message: Authority claim with no citation within 200 characters. Name the source or cut the sentence. A reviewer reads this as either unsupported or invented.
rules.notes: Citation-aware: suppressed when a citation marker follows within the same paragraph (tempered scan stops at a blank line; hard cap 400 chars). Recognises [CITE] (LaTeX \cite, substituted by stripLatex), pandoc [@key], numeric [12], and (Author, 2020) / (Author et al., 2020). Paragraph scope beats a raw character window: a claim cited two sentences later is cited, and a claim whose paragraph ends uncited is not.
rules.source: first-party observation (rigor gap: citation-audit only validates citations that exist; nothing caught an uncited authority claim) + phrase list from MIT-licensed skill corpus (stop-slop, deslop, no-ai-slop, elithrar/anti-slop — see aiism-rules.LICENSE.md)
